page: Microsoft Azure E96a_v4 is an x86_64 architecture virtual machine from the EAv4 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 96 vCPUs mapped to 48 physical cores with multi-threading enabled, powered by an AMD EPYC 7452 processor operating at 3.35 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 672.0 GB of system memory, yielding 7.0 GB of RAM per core, alongside 2458 GB of local SSD storage. No graphics processing units are included.

Performance benchmarks reveal a contrast between single-core and multi-core execution. The single-core CPU performance under stress-ng is in the bottom 10%, while multi-core performance falls into the middle 50%. However, the instance demonstrates strong capabilities in memory operations, with small-block read-only memory bandwidth and PassMark memory scores placing in the top 25%. Cryptographic performance is highly competitive, with the PassMark CPU encryption test reaching the top 10%. Redis SET operations also perform strongly at 71.0 million operations per second. Conversely, large-scale LLM inference processing is a notable bottleneck, scoring in the bottom 10%.

From a resource density perspective, the E96a_v4 provides high memory density and substantial local SSD capacity, making it a viable option for workloads that require large datasets to reside in memory without the premium of GPU hardware. Tradeoffs include lower single-threaded processing speeds and limited suitability for modern large language model inference. This server is best suited for memory-intensive applications, relational databases, caching layers such as Redis, and multi-threaded data processing tasks.
description: Microsoft Azure E96a_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine from the EAv4 family, featuring 96 vCPUs, 48 physical cores, and an AMD EPYC 7452 processor running at 3.35 GHz. It is equipped with 672.0 GB of RAM and 2458 GB of local SSD storage, managed via Microsoft Hyper-V. While single-core CPU performance and large-model LLM inference are relatively weak, the server delivers strong multi-threaded capabilities, particularly in memory bandwidth, cryptographic operations, and Redis SET throughput. The high memory-to-core ratio and integrated local SSD storage make this instance highly suitable for memory-intensive workloads, large-scale databases, and caching platforms where parallel processing and high memory capacity are critical.
